system.summary: Spanish office cipher of 1592-93: two-digit numbers carry consonant-vowel syllables, a small homophonic symbol alphabet carries bare letters, diacritics add a final consonant, and two- and three-letter groups carry the nomenclature; no. 68 is a second cipher of the same office (Feria-Mansfeld, 1593) with three-letter word codes and higher figures.

diacritics.note: Dot above = final -l, + = -m, dot after = -n, : = -r, ^ = -s, ring = -h-; bar above = the number itself; umlaut = doubled consonant; a top sign marks a code word. Confirmed on plaintext (achaque, bolsa, del passado, con).

system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's key images phelippes2.png (Spanish Cipher 1592-1593) and spanish3mansfeld.png (Feria/Mansfeld 1593), published on cryptiana as images; and the office's own key, BnF fr. 3995 fol. 97 (canvas 188), found through DECODE key records 4076 and 4077
system.notes: fr. 3995 f. 97 confirms Tomokiyo's syllable table against the original and adds the nomenclature he lacks (aunque, alli, armas, autoridad, causa, exercito, estados, election, Francia, magestad, ministro, negocios, Rey, Reyno, religion, reputacion, Roma, seignor and more). fr. 3995 f. 101 was checked and excluded: it is an Italian nomenclature belonging to another correspondence.

prior_solution.where: Keys published by Tomokiyo as images on cryptiana (spanish3.htm), reconstructed from other letters with no published reading of these four; the office's own key survives at BnF fr. 3995 f. 97 and is catalogued on DECODE as records 4076-4077; a contemporary decipherer glossed part of no. 47. No published reading of any of the four letters.

conditions.human_role: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's Spanish page fetched as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: his key tables are images, and two of them cover exactly the folios this entry cites.

The catalogue's piece numbers resolved to folios through the BnF depouillement, and the folio-to-canvas map for fr. 3983 and fr. 3984 built by reading folio numbers off top strips and interpolating; all four leaves located.

Tomokiyo's Spanish Cipher (1592-93) transcribed to key92.tsv and applied to nos. 45 and 79: Spanish comes out (supongo que hava de ser, siendo confidente, a costa de la bolsa, a los sucesores, conviene), but with holes wherever the nomenclator is used.
No. 68's figures run far higher and the leaf carries three-letter word groups, so it is the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, as Tomokiyo's citation of f. 145 says, not the cipher of the other three.

The entry's own verify step followed: DECODE returns two records for these correspondents and both are keys, not letters, pointing into BnF fr. 3995. Folio 97 is the office's own key, complete with the nomenclature Tomokiyo lacks; key92.tsv extended to 133 entries.

The contemporary interlinear gloss on no. 47 checked against the key's own output on a third letter: del Passado con, por via de mar, difiriendo de dia en dia - agreement wherever both survive, and the bar, umlaut and trailing dot settled.
All four leaves read line by line from deskewed strips: 15 of 17 lines on no. 45, 14 of 16 on no. 79, the glossed lines on no. 47, and the opening of no. 68 with keyM.tsv.
The obvious candidate for the missing Feria-Mansfeld nomenclature, fr. 3995 f. 101, fetched and excluded: it is an Italian nomenclature belonging to another correspondence.

Novelty re-examined. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. 'Never applied' replaced by 'no published reading'.
A note from satorunet (3 Oct) said the nomenclature on fr. 3995 f. 97 has over 100 word entries against the 52 word entries in key92.tsv, and that the Parme-Roy endorsement is on f. 97v, not f. 98.

f. 97 (canvas 188) and canvases 189-190 read again from the Gallica images: the endorsement is on f. 97v and says the key serves for Sessa and Ibarra; f. 98 is a French key. 61 word entries added to key92.tsv (8 numeric ones, whose number is also a syllable, kept as comments), aviso revised for causa, the rule sheet read.

Unresolved groups of nos. 45, 79, 47 rerun with the full nomenclature: 13 resolved (50T = Su Magestad, 61T = tiempo, tim = intencion, nur = ninguna, pol = duque, hus = principe, cos = personas, vur = otro), Vor corrected to opinion, and the gloss 'en particular' on no. 47 confirms zir = particular.

The 0.70 fraction_read was checked: it counted every group not marked '·' as read, so syllables that make no Spanish word counted, and it under-counted the leaves (no. 79 has 22 cipher lines, not 14; no. 47 has 21, of which 13 were read). It was not a measure of sense.

Every cipher line of nos. 45, 79 and 47 re-transcribed from 3200-3600 px Gallica crops, including the 8 untranscribed lines of no. 79 (ll. 15-22) and 8 of no. 47 (ll. 14-21); each line scored for sense in sense.tsv (measure_sense.py).

f. 97 sheet re-checked for open groups: three-dot 94 and 95 = de; three-dot 49 = Su Santidad; three-dot 88 = V.M.; three-dot 5, 8, 9, 0, 25 = nulls; ʃo = assi (not aunque, which is ʒo). These resolve groups on all three leaves (confidente de S.M., a costa de la bolsa de S.M., mostrarla a Su Santidad, assi fuesse, assi devia).

Context readings forced in several places: 9 = y (adonde, omitido y assi), xor = para (variant of xur, three occurrences), pal = duque (variant of pol; duque de Feria, duque de Mantua), 86 = vo, 'de por tes' = Desportes, 67 90 62 = Pisani. Still open in the three letters: Val, ral, ʃep, ner, ʒe, pir, mil, is, xom, mal, rili, mos, ʃer, hir, hum, us, ho, yos, ∂ir, lir, xox, ru, not on the f. 97 sheet.

no. 68 line 11 transcribed and decoded with keyM.tsv as a test: syllables but no Spanish (va le ri a no la vi o xur que le de di as se ri as ...), as on lines 7-10. Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table gives no continuous text on the body, and the nomenclature is missing; lines 12-31 were not transcribed. (Superseded the same day: the failure came from truncated transcriptions; see the next steps.)
no. 68 transcribed in full from a 3600-px crop: 20 cipher lines, 598 groups (ct68.txt); the earlier 28-line estimate was wrong.

keyM decode of ct68.txt scored with the es-golden-age 5-gram (no spaces): -2.500 per character against a maximum of -3.378 for 200 value-shuffled keys. Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table is real on this leaf and gives Spanish (a mi no me parece que puede, todo lo que se puede, pareceria que venia a ayudar, no estamos desesperados).
Unconstrained hill-climb of all numbers (anneal68.py) collapsed onto que (score -1.59, nonsense); rejected.

Constrained fill of the numbers missing from keyM (fill68.py): 57 = li accepted (top candidate, gain far above median; peligro, aliento). 64 (ha by context) not separated from na by the LM, left unread; 31, 77, 81, 95 and the 200/800 T groups undetermined. Cribs Feria, Mansfeld, Liga fit no syllable run; Paris and Su Magestad are in clear.
no. 68 scored for sense: 224/598. The new value belongs to the Mansfeld cipher, so the doubtful groups of nos. 45/79/47 (office key) gained nothing.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's cryptiana key images (Spanish Cipher 1592-93 and the Feria-Mansfeld cipher) cite these very folios (fr. 3983 ff. 98, 162; fr. 3984 f. 145), and the office's own key at BnF fr. 3995 f. 97 (DECODE R4076-R4077, returned by a search for these correspondents) supplied the nomenclator; the interlinear gloss on no. 47 checked it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: sense.tsv / measure_sense.py, 5 Oct 2026: tokens read only where they form Spanish sense; doubtful readings and code groups without a value unread. no. 45 230/254 (0.906), no. 79 504/546 (0.923), no. 47 478/510 (0.937), no. 68 224/598 (0.375, all 20 cipher lines transcribed in ct68.txt). Overall 1436/1908 = 0.753. Replaces the 0.70 of 2 Oct, which counted undotted groups rather than sense.
outcome.notes: Three letters read to about 92% of their groups on the office key (fr. 3995 f. 97), checked against the contemporary decipherment on no. 47; no. 68 is in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, which Tomokiyo's table reads (shuffled control passed) but whose nomenclature is missing: 37.5% read. codes_open counts the 22 open groups of the three letters plus the 10 Mansfeld groups named in NOTES.

gaps.detail: the three-letter nomenclature (pra, dur, hes, gar, pun, rom, mon, xen, vul, cil, var, vis, tor ...) is published nowhere and no crib fixes it; numbers 64, 31, 77, 81, 95 not separated by the LM control; diacritic finals dropped in ct68.txt
